task: S899 NCAA-DoD CARE source-system, overlap, and extraction adjudication

decision.reason: NCAA-DoD CARE is a distinct research cohort, not NCAA-ISP/NCAA ISS/High School RIO/national U.S. injury surveillance.
decision.liveOverlap: No duplicate DOI or exact CARE companion DOI is present among live papers.
decision.nonLiveOverlap: Kaminski et al. 2022 (2014-2017 CARE soccer cohort) and Jo et al. 2024 (broader CARE soccer concussion cohort) materially overlap but are not promoted live papers.

stagedFields.sourceQuote: The abstract labels this a retrospective cohort; participants were recruited into the multisite CARE study and followed under a standardised research protocol.
All 162 concussions were assigned to collision, accidental ball contact, purposeful header, or ground/object contact mechanisms; sex-specific Table 3 rows sum to 66 male and 96 female events.
For males and females, the competition incidence was 0.04 per 1000 athlete-exposures.
Practice incidence was 0.01 per 1000 athlete-exposures for males and 0.02 for females.
The results report 158 participants with one concussion and two players with two concussions during the study.

caveats: Exposure athlete-exposures were estimated by the paper, not prospectively logged; no match/training athlete-exposure totals were inferred.
The paper contains internally inconsistent sex counts; existing directly printed 1240 male and 1162 female rows were preserved.
The recurrent-event count 2 is a transparent derivation from the directly reported two players sustaining two concussions; no recurrence percentage was calculated.
Absolute male/female overall incidence, absolute incidence CIs, severity, burden, illness, and match/training counts by sex were not reported and remain blank.

rollback.path: The exact before-state rows are captured by this run and the pre-apply /tmp snapshot. Updated values and paper status can be restored from that verified copy. Additive rows or the new note would require explicit approval before deletion under repository destructive-action rules.
